On 21 January 2030 at 06.40, master potter Nakamura Seiji (68) was found dead, face down, in the display room of his workshop house in the Kamakura hills. His apprentice, Hoshino Aoi, found him and called.

A display shelf overturned, a wound on his head. The glass cabinet on the shelf open; according to the apprentice’s statement, the master’s ‘most valuable bowl’ is missing. Patrol note: “A burglar got in during the night; the old man woke and was struck or fell.”

· Inside the kiln, seven half-fired tea bowls; beside them ‘ageing’ jars filled with tea leaves and dilute acid, and four more bowls buried in the ash pit.

Cobalt… When I examined it I didn’t scrape the glaze. No one does; you don’t scrape a centuries-old bowl. It looked old. But I’ll say this: with the third bowl I had a doubt. I told Seiji. Then he doubled my fee.

Shimizu Rie — interview

The autopsy showed a bloodless, post-mortem wound and cherry-red lividity fixed on the back; the blood gas confirmed fatal carbon monoxide. The ash lines on the tatami and the sock heels showed dragging, the wildlife camera the load carried from the shed to the house, the kiln log a fire lit in the night and left untended at 02.40. The shed search tied the forgery to the master.
A scene does not always cover a crime; sometimes it covers a secret. First find where the death happened, then what the scene was hiding.
Kamakura hills — January 2030

For two years master potter Nakamura Seiji had been ageing bowls he made himself and selling them to gallerist Fujita as ‘temple heirlooms’; one went to the Kisaragi collection for forty million yen. After the buyer’s claim of forgery he went in at night to refire the new batch with an ‘old iron’ glaze in the old kiln with the cracked flue, and died of carbon monoxide in the shed with its door shut. His apprentice Hoshino Aoi, who found him at five in the morning, dragged the body to the display room to protect the master’s name, knocked over the shelf, struck his head against it and staged a burglary.
Who is responsible for Nakamura Seiji’s death?
